summary: The immutable two-commit range is scoped to the three allowed files and the broad-suite failures match baseline, but the implementation has important security, concurrency, and error-observability defects. Contractor project roots are not constrained to the authorized profile, shared runner configuration is mutated during stateless execution, and agent cleanup failures are swallowed.

evidence: gateway/run.py:21232-21239 validates only profile string equality and command presence before dispatch.
gateway/platforms/base.py:2531-2564 canonicalizes arbitrary existing absolute directories without checking authorization against the selected profile.
dimensions.assessment: The contractor path can execute with a directory that is not the registry-resolved project/profile root, violating the stated pinned-context contract.

evidence: gateway/run.py:18864-18873 dispatches any event carrying contractor_context before ordinary authorization and session bookkeeping.
gateway/run.py:21230-21236 treats a mutable boolean internal marker plus source-profile equality as sufficient authorization.
gateway/platforms/base.py:2544-2564 accepts any resolvable absolute directory, including symlink-resolved paths outside the profile.
dimensions.assessment: The trust boundary is not fail-closed. A caller able to construct an internal-looking event can direct the contractor agent into an attacker-chosen workspace and profile runtime.

evidence: gateway/run.py:21118-21119 writes contractor reasoning_config and service_tier onto the shared GatewayRunner.
gateway/run.py:9099-9103 and gateway/run.py:6352-6353 read shared service-tier state while resolving ordinary agent routes.
dimensions.assessment: Concurrent contractor and ordinary turns can overwrite each other's runner-level reasoning/service-tier state, causing cross-turn configuration contamination.

evidence: gateway/run.py:21217-21219 clears the active contractor registry entry in finally.
gateway/run.py:21251-21255 signals cancellation and invokes hard interruption.
tests/gateway/test_contractor_turns.py:376-409 covers cancellation signaling and interruption ordering.
dimensions.assessment: The cancellation path is directionally correct and sibling-safe for the tracked contractor agent, but the shared runner configuration race remains unresolved under concurrent execution.

evidence: gateway/run.py adds a large contractor-specific lifecycle directly to the already broad GatewayRunner core.
The implementation duplicates runtime resolution concerns and relies on private AIAgent fields such as _persist_disabled and _memory_enabled.
dimensions.assessment: The implementation is readable and locally cohesive, but it expands the core waist and couples the gateway to private agent internals without a narrower lifecycle abstraction.

evidence: gateway/platforms/base.py:3246 defaults close_after_turn to False, preserving ordinary persistent adapters.
gateway/platforms/base.py:7462-7467 applies clear_session only for opted-in stateless adapters or contractor events.
tests/gateway/test_contractor_turns.py:231-258 verifies ordinary events remain on the existing session path.
dimensions.assessment: The ordinary persistent-session path remains guarded by the existing default and the focused negative test covers the principal bypass concern.

evidence: tests/gateway/test_contractor_turns.py contains 24 focused tests covering validation, skill ordering, cancellation, memory-tool rejection, cleanup, and ordinary-turn negatives.
No focused test covers project-root containment, symlink escape, forged internal origin, concurrent shared runtime configuration, or cleanup failure propagation.
dimensions.assessment: The focused suite is substantial but misses the highest-risk security and concurrency cases identified in the source review.

evidence: gateway/run.py:21217-21219 invokes _cleanup_agent_resources in finally.
gateway/run.py:12378-12425 catches exceptions from shutdown_memory_provider and close() and suppresses them.
The contractor caller therefore cannot distinguish successful teardown from leaked resources.
dimensions.assessment: Cleanup failures required to remain observable are converted into silent success; a primary model error can also be obscured diagnostically because teardown failure is discarded.

evidence: The preserved differential artifact reports identical eight failing gateway node IDs and error classes at base and head, with zero branch-only failures.
git diff --check for the immutable range passed.
The final worktree status was clean and the range contains exactly two commits.
dimensions.assessment: The broad-suite failures are baseline-only according to the supplied exact node-ID and error-class comparison; they do not explain the introduced findings.

findings.title: Contractor project root is not constrained to the authorized profile
findings.description: ContractorTurnContext resolves and stores any existing absolute directory, including symlink-resolved directories outside the selected profile. _handle_contractor_turn later uses context.project_root as the worker CWD while only checking source.profile == context.profile_name; it never proves that the root belongs to the registry-resolved profile or canonical project.
findings.impact: An internal caller that can fabricate a contractor-shaped event can run the agent in an attacker-chosen workspace, exposing files and allowing tools to operate outside the authorized project boundary. The pre-session dispatch makes this occur before ordinary authorization and persistence guards.
findings.required_fix: Resolve the authorized profile/project root from trusted registry state and require the context root to equal or be safely contained within that canonical root, rejecting symlink escapes and mismatches. Do not treat arbitrary event-supplied internal context as sufficient authorization.

findings.title: Contractor execution mutates shared runner runtime state
findings.description: Each contractor worker assigns self._reasoning_config and self._service_tier before calling _resolve_turn_agent_config. Those attributes are shared by GatewayRunner and are read by ordinary and background agent route resolution, so concurrent turns can overwrite values between resolution and AIAgent construction.
findings.impact: A contractor invocation can inherit an ordinary turn's service tier or alter an ordinary turn's request routing, violating sibling isolation and potentially changing provider behavior, cost, or latency without the affected turn's configuration.
findings.required_fix: Keep reasoning configuration and service tier local to the contractor invocation and pass them explicitly through route resolution and AIAgent construction. Remove the contractor path's writes to shared runner attributes.

findings.title: Contractor cleanup failures are silently discarded
findings.description: The contractor finally block calls _cleanup_agent_resources, whose shutdown_memory_provider and agent.close exceptions are caught and ignored. No error or status is returned to the caller when teardown fails, even though the contractor path is responsible for deterministic cleanup and cache/resource eviction.
findings.impact: A successful-looking contractor result can leave tool subprocesses, clients, or provider resources alive, while cancellation or model errors provide no observable indication that cleanup also failed. This prevents operators and callers from detecting resource leaks.
findings.required_fix: Use a contractor-specific cleanup result/error path that logs and surfaces cleanup failures without replacing an existing primary exception; preserve the primary execution result/error while attaching cleanup failure observability.
